## Scope and provenance

This self-contained document combines the original full session, marked human interventions,
their retrospective rationale annotations, the earlier annotation snapshot, and yesterday's
live-evaluation evidence. It contains no implementation or evaluation from the later repair attempt.
All 405 exported messages and their ordered tool-call/result parts are preserved.

The annotations and consolidation were prepared retrospectively on 2026-11-23 with Codex
assistance. They summarize actual user messages; they do not create new historical approvals.
The student identity was confirmed by Xia Yue outside the original OpenCode session.
The original user messages remain the authority for what was approved or prohibited.

## Complete original messages, with marked interventions

<a id="message-001"></a>

### 001 — user — msg_2020253550012c85n6QJR6Rl20

**Marked human intervention — Xia Yue (60472258)**

- Action: Define scope and require read-only planning
- Rationale (retrospective summary): Preserve FEAT-01, speaker order, round caps and the separate risk debate; review the plan before any edits.
- Evidence: the original user message reproduced immediately below.

**Original user wording (verbatim):**

```text
Plan FEAT-02 (FR-DEB-01): research-debate early stopping.

Our team works directly on the existing CS5351 branch. Stay on this branch; do not create a branch or worktree. First confirm the working directory, current HEAD, branch and working-tree status using read-only commands. Preserve the completed FEAT-01 Options Analyst implementation. Flag stale baseline references rather than resetting the repository.


Read AGENTS.md and Prompt.md first and follow their reading order. Locate FR-DEB-01, the FEAT-02 architecture section, trace matrix, relevant constraints, and acceptance cases DEB-T1 through DEB-T5.


Required behavior:
- Apply early stopping only to the research bull/bear debate.
- One round means one bull turn and one bear turn.
- Do not stop the opening round for lack of progress.
- From round two onward, assess progress only after both researchers have spoken.
- Continue within the configured cap if either side introduces new evidence or gives a first substantive reply to a previously unanswered opposing argument. Rephrasing an existing fact or rebuttal is not progress.
- Otherwise, record the specified early-stop reason and pass the complete debate history to the Research Manager.
- Keep the configured round cap binding and give it priority.
- Preserve FEAT-01 options-report delivery, unavailable-data handling, existing entry points and the separate risk-debate behavior.


The progress-detection method is unresolved. Propose a concrete approach, explain its limitations and uncertainty/failure handling, and identify any additional model calls or token costs. Do not assume FEAT-05 paragraph citations already exist.


Return a concise plan covering:
1. Completion criteria and current implementation.
2. Editable and frozen paths, affected interfaces and state.
3. Progress-detection design and decisions requiring my review.
4. DEB-T1–T5 coverage, negative cases and FEAT-01 regression checks. Cover both progress detection and routing.
5. Ordered implementation steps, environment prerequisites and verification commands.


This stage is read-only planning. Do not modify files, install dependencies, commit or push. Stop for my plan review. After plan approval, write tests only and obtain separate explicit test approval before implementing the feature.
```

        "output": "<path>E:\\CityU课程材料\\CS5351软工\\CS5351-Project\\TradingAgents\\docs\\code-governance\\verification-constraints.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Verification constraints\n2: \n3: Reference a requirement or invariant in each new test. Cover every fit criterion and include a violation test for each invariant and a negative test per feature. Have a human approve the proposed tests before implementation.\n4: \n5: Verify structural boundaries and permissions, run all previous regression suites, and measure behavior against approved thresholds. Record failures and rerun evidence in the review memo.\n6: \n7: ## Options Analyst — proposed offline acceptance cases\n8: \n9: Review and approve these cases before implementation. Use fixed option-chain observations, a recording model and the existing offline graph. Each case below describes expected evidence.\n10: \n11: | Case | Setup and assertion |\n12: | --- | --- |\n13: | OPT-T1 · FR-OPT-01 | Check fresh CLI and Python stock defaults include exactly the original four plus options. Repeat with explicit options-only and original-four selections, including saved preferences. Verify selected nodes match exactly. With options off, count zero options fetches, calls and exported sections. |\n14: | OPT-T2 · FR-OPT-02 | Supply an eligible option-chain observation with a distinctive expiry, strike and quoted value. Assert exactly one independent report for the selected stock/date and check its evidence against the fixture. Inspect the analyst input for the option-chain observation. |\n15: | OPT-T3 · FR-OPT-03 | Tag the options report. Capture the actual model inputs for the bull, bear, aggressive, neutral and conservative roles and check all five for the tag. Repeat with only options selected. Trace scripted debate and plan outputs through the managers and trader to a decision. |\n16: | OPT-T4 · FR-OPT-04 | Use the tagged report. Check CLI completion and report panel, final state and saved JSON log. Exercise CLI and Python export and check the individual Markdown file, combined Markdown and requested HTML. Reopen a baseline output without the new field. |\n17: | OPT-T5 · FR-OPT-05 | Replay an empty chain, unavailable provider and historical date without an eligible snapshot. Each run must expose the unavailable notice to all five direct consumers, show and save that notice, and produce a final decision. Check the notice carries no inferred options signal. |\n18: | OPT-T6 · INV-OPT-01 | Inject a later snapshot into a historical run. Also exercise wrong-symbol and unknown-time records. Capture the adapter output: zero invalid observations may enter the analyst context. In a mixed fixture retain eligible observations, including one at the cutoff. With only rejected records verify the OPT-T5 fallback. |\n19: \n20: Run the full prior offline suite alongside these cases in the implementation PR. Live-provider checks depend on provider selection and credentials.\n21: \n22: ## FEAT-02 — Research debate early stop (FR-DEB-01)\n23: \n24: Proposed offline cases. Use scripted researcher turns and inspect the route after each turn.\n25: For every termination, compare the Research Manager's input history with the full scripted exchange through the last bear turn.\n26: \n27: | Case | Fixed exchange | Expected outcome |\n28: | --- | --- | --- |\n29: | DEB-T1 | Limit 3. Both sides state opening positions without citing evidence or answering a point. | Bull and bear each speak once. Round two begins. |\n30: | DEB-T2 | Limit 3. In round two both repeat round-one facts and rephrase a rebuttal already made. | The bear still gets its turn. Stop after round two, record the no-progress reason and hand off without starting round three. |\n31: | DEB-T3 | Limit 3. In round two one side cites a report fact unused in round one. Neither side answers a new point. | Begin round three. |\n32: | DEB-T4 | Limit 3. Round two adds no facts, but one side addresses a specific opposing argument left unanswered in round one. | Begin round three. |\n33: | DEB-T5 | Run with limit 1, then with limit 2 and fresh evidence in round two. | Hand off after exactly one and two complete rounds respectively. The configured cap applies in both cases. |\n34: \n35: ## FEAT-03 — Company background (FR-RPT-01)\n36: \n37: Proposed offline cases. Use fixed profile data and exercise the existing CLI and Python export paths. Compare the visible section text across formats.\n38: \n39: | Case | Input | Expected export |\n40: | --- | --- | --- |\n41: | RPT-T1 | Full profile with a name, industry and two-sentence description. Omit Fundamentals Analyst from the selection. | Each format contains one background section after the header and before the analyst reports. Both show the fixture fields and the same description. |\n42: | RPT-T2 | Profile contains only a company name. | Both sections show just the name. The rest of the report exports successfully. |\n43: | RPT-T3 | No profile fields are available. | Both sections show an unavailable notice. The analysis and final decision still appear in the export. |\n44: | RPT-T4 | Historical analysis with only a current name, current industry and current business description. | Both sections label the name as current and omit the undated industry and business description. |\n45: \n46: ## FEAT-04 — Per-run token usage warning (FR-TOK-01)\n47: \n48: Proposed offline cases. Feed scripted usage metadata from multiple agents through each entry point. Capture terminal warnings for CLI runs and browser activity warnings for web runs.\n49: \n50: | Case | Setup | Expected outcome |\n51: | --- | --- | --- |\n52: | TOK-T1 | Set the threshold to 1000. Supply input/output pairs (700, 200), (80, 20), (60, 40) and (100, 100). | Cumulative totals are 900, 1000, 1100 and 1300. Exactly one warning appears, at 1100, showing 1100 used and a threshold of 1000. The final report is produced. |\n53: | TOK-T2 | Leave the threshold unset. Run two analyses in the same process. In each, reach 100000, receive one completion with no usage metadata, then add one reported token. | Each analysis starts at zero, stays quiet through 100000, and warns once at 100001 with the default threshold of 100000. |\n54: \n55: ## FEAT-05 — Paragraph citations (FR-CIT-01)\n56: \n57: Use fixed analyst reports and scripted turns. Inspect both researcher inputs and the exported Markdown and HTML. These cases are proposed for review before implementation.\n58: \n59: | Case | Setup | Expected outcome |\n60: | --- | --- | --- |\n61: | CIT-T1 | Supply a fundamentals report with a heading and two distinct body paragraphs separated by a blank line. Bull cites the first and bear the second. Repeat with an options report added to the inputs. | Both researchers see FUN-01 and FUN-02 on the same original paragraphs in both runs. The heading has no ID. The options report starts at OPT-01. Each export contains one matching source paragraph per citation, with the ID also beside the correct argument. |\n62: | CIT-T2 | Script a claim citing two valid paragraphs, one citing an absent FUN-99, and one with no citation. | Both valid references remain beside the first claim. Check the total and mark the first crossing under the handler's existing lock so simultaneous completions produce a single warning. Send the crossing total and configured threshold to the active terminal or browser activity view. The graph continues normally.\n\nThe run-level warning threshold is independent of `TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_TOKENS`, which controls output length per model call.\n\n## FEAT-05 — Paragraph citations in the research debate\n\nAt the handoff from analysts to researchers, assign a stable report prefix and a sequence starting at 01 within each supplied report. For example, `[MKT-01]` identifies the first market paragraph and `[FUN-02]` the second fundamentals paragraph. Treat blank lines as body paragraph boundaries and skip headings and empty blocks. Preserve the original paragraph text. A selected Options Analyst report uses its own sequence (`OPT`). The company background added at export falls outside the debate inputs.\n\nGive both researchers the same labelled text. Each argument carries the ID or IDs for its evidence. Before recording a turn, check each ID against this run's paragraphs. Display “Invalid citation” beside unknown IDs and “No citation provided” beside an argument with none. Preserve these annotations in the debate history and continue. Both consolidated renderers use the original labels so a reader can search for the cited source.\n\nFEAT-02 evaluates progress separately. A first reply to an unanswered opposing point can advance the debate even when both speakers cite the same paragraph.\n\n## FEAT-06 — Local web interface (specified)\n\nThe planned `tradingagents web` entry point serves one local user. Print the local URL and open the default browser after the service is ready. The printed URL also works when automatic opening fails. The existing CLI command continues to open the terminal interface.\n\n| Handoff | Contract |\n| --- | --- |\n| Form to run | Reuse CLI validation, provider/model choices, analyst defaults and graph configuration. Read credentials on the host. Disable Start during an active run and accept only one start for that run. |\n| Run to browser | Consume the existing graph stream that feeds the CLI. Show agent status, messages and tool calls in the activity view. In the content view preserve analyst reports, individual bull/bear turns, the research manager's plan, trader proposal, all three risk opinions and the final decision. Append new content in observed order and suppress duplicate items from cumulative snapshots. |\n| Feature interactions | FEAT-01 supplies options selection and report or unavailable notice. FEAT-02 supplies the early-stop reason before the manager takes over. FEAT-04 supplies token totals and its single threshold warning. FEAT-05 supplies paragraph IDs, inline citations and validation notices during the debate. |\n| Run to results | Use the existing report writer for this run's HTML preview and Markdown download, including FEAT-03 company background and FEAT-05 source labels.             "text": "from tradingagents.agents.state import AgentState\n\n\nclass ConditionalLogic:\n    \"\"\"Handles conditional logic for determining graph flow.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, max_debate_rounds=1, max_risk_discuss_rounds=1):\n        \"\"\"Initialize with configuration parameters.\"\"\"\n        self.max_debate_rounds = max_debate_rounds\n        self.max_risk_discuss_rounds = max_risk_discuss_rounds\n\n    def should_continue_debate(self, state: AgentState) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Determine if debate should continue.\"\"\"\n\n        if (\n            state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"count\"] >= 2 * self.max_debate_rounds\n        ):  # max_debate_rounds turns each for bull and bear\n            return \"Research Manager\"\n        if state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"current_response\"].startswith(\"Bull\"):\n            return \"Bear Researcher\"\n        return \"Bull Researcher\"\n\n    def should_continue_risk_analysis(self, state: AgentState) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Determine if risk analysis should continue.\"\"\"\n        if (\n            state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"count\"] >= 3 * self.max_risk_discuss_rounds\n        ):  # max_risk_discuss_rounds turns each for the three risk analysts\n            return \"Portfolio Manager\"\n        if state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"latest_speaker\"].startswith(\"Aggressive\"):\n            return \"Conservative Analyst\"\n        if state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"latest_speaker\"].startswith(\"Conservative\"):\n            return \"Neutral Analyst\"\n        return \"Aggressive Analyst\"",

            "text": "from tradingagents.agents.context import (\n    get_instrument_context_from_state,\n    get_language_instruction,\n    opponent_argument_or_opening,\n    report_or_absent,\n)\n\n\ndef create_bull_researcher(llm):\n    def bull_node(state) -> dict:\n        investment_debate_state = state[\"investment_debate_state\"]\n        history = investment_debate_state.get(\"history\", \"\")\n        bull_history = investment_debate_state.get(\"bull_history\", \"\")\n\n        current_response = opponent_argument_or_opening(\n            investment_debate_state.get(\"current_response\", \"\"), \"bear analyst\"\n        )\n        market_research_report = report_or_absent(state[\"market_report\"], \"market\")\n        sentiment_report = report_or_absent(state[\"sentiment_report\"], \"sentiment\")\n        news_report = report_or_absent(state[\"news_report\"], \"news\")\n        fundamentals_report = report_or_absent(state[\"fundamentals_report\"], \"fundamentals\")\n        options_report = report_or_absent(state.get(\"options_report\", \"\"), \"options\")\n        instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n        asset_type = state.get(\"asset_type\", \"stock\")\n        target_label = \"stock\" if asset_type == \"stock\" else \"asset\"\n        fundamentals_label = (\n            \"Company fundamentals report\"\n            if asset_type == \"stock\"\n            else \"Asset fundamentals report (may be unavailable for crypto)\"\n        )\n\n        prompt = f\"\"\"You are a Bull Analyst advocating for investing in the {target_label}. Your task is to build a strong, evidence-based case emphasizing growth potential, competitive advantages, and positive market indicators. Leverage the provided research and data to address concerns and counter bearish arguments effectively.\n\nKey points to focus on:\n- Growth Potential: Highlight the company's market opportunities, revenue projections, and scalability.\n- Competitive Advantages: Emphasize factors like unique products, strong branding, or dominant market positioning.\n- Positive Indicators: Use financial health, industry trends, and recent positive news as evidence.\n- Bear Counterpoints: Critically analyze the bear argument with specific data and sound reasoning, addressing concerns thoroughly and showing why the bull perspective holds stronger merit.\n- Engagement: Present your argument in a conversational style, engaging directly with the bear analyst's points and debating effectively rather than just listing data.\n\nResources available:\n{instrument_context}\nMarket research report: {market_research_report}\nSocial media sentiment report: {sentiment_report}\nLatest world affairs news: {news_report}\n{fundamentals_label}: {fundamentals_report}\nOptions market report: {options_report}\nConversation history of the debate: {history}\nLast bear argument: {current_response}\nUse this information to deliver a compelling bull argument, refute the bear's concerns, and engage in a dynamic debate that demonstrates the strengths of the bull position.\n\"\"\" + get_language_instruction()\n\n        response = llm.invoke(prompt)\n\n        argument = f\"Bull Analyst: {response.content}\"\n\n        new_investment_debate_state = {\n            \"history\": history + \"\\n\" + argument,\n            \"bull_history\": bull_history + \"\\n\" + argument,\n            \"bear_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bear_history\", \"\"),\n            \"current_response\": argument,\n            \"count\": investment_debate_state[\"count\"] + 1,\n        }\n\n        return {\"investment_debate_state\": new_investment_debate_state}\n\n    return bull_node",

        "output": "<path>E:\\CityU课程材料\\CS5351软工\\CS5351-Project\\TradingAgents\\src\\tradingagents\\agents\\managers\\research_manager.py</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: \"\"\"Research Manager: turns the bull/bear debate into a structured investment plan for the trader.\"\"\"\n2: \n3: from __future__ import annotations\n4: \n5: from tradingagents.agents.context import get_instrument_context_from_state, get_language_instruction\n6: from tradingagents.agents.schemas import ResearchPlan, render_research_plan\n7: from tradingagents.agents.structured import (\n8:     NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS,\n9:     bind_structured,\n10:     invoke_structured_or_freetext,\n11: )\n12: \n13: \n14: def create_research_manager(llm):\n15:     structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, ResearchPlan, \"Research Manager\")\n16: \n17:     def research_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n18:         instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n19:         history = state[\"investment_debate_state\"].get(\"history\", \"\")\n20: \n21:         investment_debate_state = state[\"investment_debate_state\"]\n22: \n23:         prompt = f\"\"\"As the Research Manager and debate facilitator, your role is to critically evaluate this round of debate and deliver a clear, actionable investment plan for the trader.\n24: \n25: {instrument_context}\n26: \n27: ---\n28: \n29: **Rating Scale** (use exactly one):\n30: - **Buy**: Strong conviction in the bull thesis; recommend taking or growing the position\n31: - **Overweight**: Constructive view; recommend gradually increasing exposure\n32: - **Hold**: Balanced view; recommend maintaining the current position\n33: - **Underweight**: Cautious view; recommend trimming exposure\n34: - **Sell**: Strong conviction in the bear thesis; recommend exiting or avoiding the position\n35: \n36: The debate always contains conflicting arguments; deciding which side is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the side with the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not manufacture a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the bull and bear cases on their merits, independent of which side spoke first or last.\n37: \n38: ---\n39: \n40: **Debate History:**\n41: {history}\n42: \n43: ## Output\n44: \n45: Write these sections, in this order, starting with the recommendation on its own line:\n46: \n47: - **Recommendation**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell\n48: - **Rationale**: which arguments decided it\n49: - **Strategic Actions**: concrete steps for the trader, sized against a standard allocation\n50: \n51: {NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS}\"\"\" + get_language_instruction()\n52: \n53:         investment_plan = invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n54:             structured_llm,\n55:             llm,\n56:             prompt,\n57:             render_research_plan,\n58:             \"Research Manager\",\n59:         )\n60: \n61:         new_investment_debate_state = {\n62:             \"history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"history\", \"\"),\n63:             \"bear_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bear_history\", \"\"),\n64:             \"bull_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bull_history\", \"\"),\n65:             \"current_response\": investment_plan,\n66:             \"count\": investment_debate_state[\"count\"],\n67:         }\n68: \n69:         return {\n70:             \"investment_debate_state\": new_investment_debate_state,\n71:             \"investment_plan\": investment_plan,\n72:         }\n73: \n74:     return research_manager_node\n\n(End of file - total 74 lines)\n</content>",

          "preview": "\"\"\"Research Manager: turns the bull/bear debate into a structured investment plan for the trader.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.context import get_instrument_context_from_state, get_language_instruction\nfrom tradingagents.agents.schemas import ResearchPlan, render_research_plan\nfrom tradingagents.agents.structured import (\n    NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS,\n    bind_structured,\n    invoke_structured_or_freetext,\n)\n\n\ndef create_research_manager(llm):\n    structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, ResearchPlan, \"Research Manager\")\n\n    def research_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n        instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n        history = state[\"investment_debate_state\"].get(\"history\", \"\")\n",

            "path": "E:\\CityU课程材料\\CS5351软工\\CS5351-Project\\TradingAgents\\src\\tradingagents\\agents\\managers\\research_manager.py",
            "text": "\"\"\"Research Manager: turns the bull/bear debate into a structured investment plan for the trader.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.context import get_instrument_context_from_state, get_language_instruction\nfrom tradingagents.agents.schemas import ResearchPlan, render_research_plan\nfrom tradingagents.agents.structured import (\n    NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS,\n    bind_structured,\n    invoke_structured_or_freetext,\n)\n\n\ndef create_research_manager(llm):\n    structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, ResearchPlan, \"Research Manager\")\n\n    def research_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n        instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n        history = state[\"investment_debate_state\"].get(\"history\", \"\")\n\n        investment_debate_state = state[\"investment_debate_state\"]\n\n        prompt = f\"\"\"As the Research Manager and debate facilitator, your role is to critically evaluate this round of debate and deliver a clear, actionable investment plan for the trader.\n\n{instrument_context}\n\n---\n\n**Rating Scale** (use exactly one):\n- **Buy**: Strong conviction in the bull thesis; recommend taking or growing the position\n- **Overweight**: Constructive view; recommend gradually increasing exposure\n- **Hold**: Balanced view; recommend maintaining the current position\n- **Underweight**: Cautious view; recommend trimming exposure\n- **Sell**: Strong conviction in the bear thesis; recommend exiting or avoiding the position\n\nThe debate always contains conflicting arguments; deciding which side is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the side with the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not manufacture a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the bull and bear cases on their merits, independent of which side spoke first or last.\n\n---\n\n**Debate History:**\n{history}\n\n## Output\n\nWrite these sections, in this order, starting with the recommendation on its own line:\n\n- **Recommendation**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell\n- **Rationale**: which arguments decided it\n- **Strategic Actions**: concrete steps for the trader, sized against a standard allocation\n\n{NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS}\"\"\" + get_language_instruction()\n\n        investment_plan = invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n            structured_llm,\n            llm,\n            prompt,\n            render_research_plan,\n            \"Research Manager\",\n        )\n\n        new_investment_debate_state = {\n            \"history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"history\", \"\"),\n            \"bear_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bear_history\", \"\"),\n            \"bull_history\": investment_debate_state.get(\"bull_history\", \"\"),\n            \"current_response\": investment_plan,\n            \"count\": investment_debate_state[\"count\"],\n        }\n\n        return {\n            \"investment_debate_state\": new_investment_debate_state,\n            \"investment_plan\": investment_plan,\n        }\n\n    return research_manager_node",

Researcher team state\n8: class InvestDebateState(TypedDict):\n9:     bull_history: Annotated[\n10:         str, \"Bullish Conversation history\"\n11:     ]\n12:     bear_history: Annotated[\n13:         str, \"Bearish Conversation history\"\n14:     ]\n15:     history: Annotated[str, \"Conversation history\"]\n16:     current_response: Annotated[str, \"Latest response\"]\n17:     count: Annotated[int, \"Length of the current conversation\"]\n18: \n19: \n20: # Risk management team state\n21: class RiskDebateState(TypedDict):\n22:     aggressive_history: Annotated[\n23:         str, \"Aggressive Agent's Conversation history\"\n24:     ]\n25:     conservative_history: Annotated[\n26:         str, \"Conservative Agent's Conversation history\"\n27:     ]\n28:     neutral_history: Annotated[\n29:         str, \"Neutral Agent's Conversation history\"\n30:     ]\n31:     history: Annotated[str, \"Conversation history\"]\n32:     latest_speaker: Annotated[str, \"Analyst that spoke last\"]\n33:     current_aggressive_response: Annotated[\n34:         str, \"Latest response by the aggressive analyst\"\n35:     ]\n36:     current_conservative_response: Annotated[\n37:         str, \"Latest response by the conservative analyst\"\n38:     ]\n39:     current_neutral_response: Annotated[\n40:         str, \"Latest response by the neutral analyst\"\n41:     ]\n42:     count: Annotated[int, \"Length of the current conversation\"]\n43: \n44: \n45: class AgentState(MessagesState):\n46:     company_of_interest: Annotated[str, \"Company that we are interested in trading\"]\n47:     asset_type: Annotated[str, \"Asset type under analysis such as stock or crypto\"]\n48:     instrument_context: Annotated[str, \"Deterministic ticker identity resolved at run start\"]\n49:     trade_date: Annotated[str, \"The analysis date; data is served as of it\"]\n50: \n51:     # research step\n52:     market_report: Annotated[str, \"Report from the Market Analyst\"]\n53:     sentiment_report: Annotated[str, \"Report from the Sentiment Analyst\"]\n54:     news_report: Annotated[str, \"Report from the News Analyst on company and world news\"]\n55:     fundamentals_report: Annotated[str, \"Report from the Fundamentals Analyst\"]\n56:     options_report: Annotated[str, \"Report from the Options Analyst, or its unavailable notice\"]\n57: \n58:     # researcher team discussion step\n59:     investment_debate_state: Annotated[\n60:         InvestDebateState, \"Current state of the debate on if to invest or not\"\n61:     ]\n62:     investment_plan: Annotated[str, \"Investment plan from the Research Manager\"]\n63: \n64:     trader_investment_plan: Annotated[str, \"Transaction proposal from the Trader\"]\n65: \n66:     # risk management team discussion step\n67:     risk_debate_state: Annotated[\n68:         RiskDebateState, \"Current state of the debate on evaluating risk\"\n69:     ]\n70:     final_trade_decision: Annotated[str, \"Final decision from the Portfolio Manager\"]\n71:     final_rating: Annotated[str, \"The Portfolio Manager's 5-tier rating, or REVIEW when it has none\"]\n72:     past_context: Annotated[str, \"Memory log context for the Portfolio Manager (same-ticker decisions + cross-ticker lessons), written by the Memory Log step\"]\n73:     memory_note: Annotated[str, \"What the Memory Log step could not settle or read this run, for the report; empty when all went well\"]\n74:     portfolio_context: Annotated[str, \"Caller-supplied holdings and cash, rendered at run start; empty when not provided\"]\n\n(End of file - total 74 lines)\n</content>",

A failure here\n        does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in\n        the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.\n        \"\"\"\n        note = \"\"\n        try:\n            # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.\n            done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)\n            if done.failed:\n                note = (f\"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run \"\n                        \"and stay pending.\")\n        except Exception as exc:\n            logger.warning(\"Settling past decisions failed: %s\", exc)\n            note = f\"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending.\"\n        try:\n            past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(\n                state[\"company_of_interest\"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state[\"trade_date\"]))\n        except Exception as exc:\n            logger.warning(\"Reading the memory log failed: %s\", exc)\n            past_context = \"\"\n            note = note or f\"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__}).\"\n        return {\"past_context\": past_context, \"memory_note\": note}\n\n    def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:\n        \"\"\"Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.\n\n        A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own\n        decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done\n        analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to\n        settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.\n        \"\"\"\n        with run_config(self.config):\n            return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)\n\n    def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:\n        \"\"\"Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).\n\n        For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would\n        otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.\n        With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.\n        \"\"\"\n        with run_config(self.config):\n            return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)\n\n    def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):\n        \"\"\"Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log\n        for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here.\"\"\"\n        self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)\n        decision = final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\")\n        if not decision:\n            logger.warning(\"No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log\",\n                           company_name, trade_date)\n            return\n        self.memory_log.store_decision(\n            ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,\n            rating=run_rating(final_state),\n        )\n\n    def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n                   checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):\n        \"\"\"Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log.\"\"\"\n        init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n        args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()\n\n        # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same\n        # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).\n        if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:\n            args.setdefault(\"config\", {}).setdefault(\"configurable\", {})[\"thread_id\"] = checkpoint_thread_id\n\n        # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).\n        graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)\n        if self.debug:\n            # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).\n            final_state, printed = {}, set()\n            for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):\n                for msg in messages:\n                    key = getattr(msg, \"id\", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, \"content\", None))\n                    if key not in printed:\n                        printed.add(key)\n                        msg.pretty_print()\n                if state is not None:\n                    final_state.update(state)\n        else:\n            final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)\n\n        self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)\n\n        # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state.\n        self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n\n        return final_state, run_rating(final_state)\n\n    def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):\n        \"\"\"Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.\n\n        ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``\n        is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's\n        graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.\n\n        Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the\n        analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages\n        and reports come from their own finished steps (\"tasks\") as they happen.\n        \"\"\"\n        args = {**args, \"stream_mode\": [\"values\", \"tasks\"]}\n        # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even\n        # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the\n        # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.\n        context = run_config_context(self.config)\n        stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)\n        try:\n            while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:\n                namespace, mode, chunk = step\n                if namespace:\n                    result = chunk.get(\"result\") if mode == \"tasks\" else None\n                    if isinstance(result, dict):\n                        report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != \"messages\" and v}\n                        if result.get(\"messages\") or report:\n                            yield result.get(\"messages\", []), report or None\n                elif mode == \"values\":\n                    yield chunk.get(\"messages\", []), chunk\n        finally:\n            context.run(stream.close)\n\n    def _log_state(self, trade_date, final_state):\n        \"\"\"Write a run's final state to JSON under the run's own ticker.\"\"\"\n        entry = {\n            \"company_of_interest\": final_state[\"company_of_interest\"],\n            \"trade_date\": final_state[\"trade_date\"],\n            \"market_report\": final_state[\"market_report\"],\n            \"sentiment_report\": final_state[\"sentiment_report\"],\n            \"news_report\": final_state[\"news_report\"],\n            \"fundamentals_report\": final_state[\"fundamentals_report\"],\n            \"options_report\": final_state.get(\"options_report\", \"\"),\n            \"investment_debate_state\": {\n                \"bull_history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"bull_history\"],\n                \"bear_history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"bear_history\"],\n                \"history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"history\"],\n                \"current_response\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\n                    \"current_response\"\n                ],\n            },\n            \"trader_investment_plan\": final_state[\"trader_investment_plan\"],\n            \"risk_debate_state\": {\n                \"aggressive_history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"aggressive_history\"],\n                \"conservative_history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"conservative_history\"],\n                \"neutral_history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"neutral_history\"],\n                \"history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"history\"],\n            },\n            \"investment_plan\": final_state[\"investment_plan\"],\n            \"final_trade_decision\": final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"],\n            \"final_rating\": run_rating(final_state),\n            \"run_settings\": self.run_settings(),\n        }\n\n        # A ticker that would escape the results directory is rejected.\n        safe_ticker = safe_ticker_component(final_state[\"company_of_interest\"])\n        directory = Path(self.config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker / \"TradingAgentsStrategy_logs\"\n        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n        log_path = directory / f\"full_states_log_{trade_date}.json\"\n        with open(log_path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            # Reports can be in any language and this file is read by a person.\n            json.dump(entry, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False)",

After\n59:     ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and\n60:     that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools\n61:     cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).\n62:     \"\"\"\n63:     output = TypedDict(f\"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report\", {spec.report_key: str})\n64:     graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n65:     graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n66:     graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n67:     if not spec.tools:\n68:         graph.add_edge(\"agent\", END)\n69:         return graph.compile()\n70: \n71:     def calls(messages):\n72:         return [call[\"name\"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None) or [])]\n73: \n74:     def rounds(messages) -> int:\n75:         return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n76: \n77:     def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n78:         return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n79: \n80:     def wrap_up(state):\n81:         repeated = \", \".join(f\"{name} x{n}\" for name, n in Counter(calls(state[\"messages\"])).most_common())\n82:         logger.warning(\"%s used its %d tool rounds (%s);             "text": "import logging\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Any, TypedDict\n\nfrom langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage\nfrom langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph\nfrom langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents import (\n    create_aggressive_debator,\n    create_bear_researcher,\n    create_bull_researcher,\n    create_conservative_debator,\n    create_fundamentals_analyst,\n    create_market_analyst,\n    create_neutral_debator,\n    create_news_analyst,\n    create_options_analyst,\n    create_portfolio_manager,\n    create_research_manager,\n    create_sentiment_analyst,\n    create_trader,\n)\nfrom tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\nfrom tradingagents.agents.state import AgentState\n\nfrom .analyst_execution import build_analyst_execution_plan\nfrom .conditional_logic import ConditionalLogic\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n# Every target a shared conditional router can return. Each edge driven by the\n# router maps all of them, so a fall-through return (e.g. under prompt/i18n/\n# refactor drift in the speaker labels) can never hit a missing path_map entry\n# and crash LangGraph mid-run (#1088).\nDEBATE_PATH_MAP = {\n    \"Bull Researcher\": \"Bull Researcher\",\n    \"Bear Researcher\": \"Bear Researcher\",\n    \"Research Manager\": \"Research Manager\",\n}\nRISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP = {\n    \"Aggressive Analyst\": \"Aggressive Analyst\",\n    \"Conservative Analyst\": \"Conservative Analyst\",\n    \"Neutral Analyst\": \"Neutral Analyst\",\n    \"Portfolio Manager\": \"Portfolio Manager\",\n}\n\n\ndef _tools_or_done(state) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Route an analyst's turn: run its tool calls, or finish with its report.\"\"\"\n    return \"tools\" if state[\"messages\"][-1].tool_calls else END\n\n\ndef _analyst_graph(spec, agent, max_tool_rounds: int):\n    \"\"\"One analyst as a graph of its own: the model and its tools, on a private message history.\n\n    It returns only its report, so analysts running side by side never write the\n    same key, and its tool calls never reach the other analysts' messages. After\n    ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and\n    that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools\n    cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).\n    \"\"\"\n    output = TypedDict(f\"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report\", {spec.report_key: str})\n    graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n    graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n    graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n    if not spec.tools:\n        graph.add_edge(\"agent\", END)\n        return graph.compile()\n\n    def calls(messages):\n        return [call[\"name\"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None) or [])]\n\n    def rounds(messages) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n\n    def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n        return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n\n    def wrap_up(state):\n        repeated = \", \".join(f\"{name} x{n}\" for name, n in Counter(calls(state[\"messages\"])).most_common())\n        logger.warning(\"%s used its %d tool rounds (%s); asking for its report\",\n                       spec.agent_node, max_tool_rounds, repeated)\n        return agent({**state, \"messages\": [*state[\"messages\"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})\n\n    graph.add_node(\"tools\", ToolNode(list(spec.tools)))\n    graph.add_node(\"wrap_up\", wrap_up)\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"agent\", _tools_or_done, [\"tools\", END])\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"tools\", more_or_wrap_up, [\"agent\", \"wrap_up\"])\n    graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", END)\n    return graph.compile()\n\n\nclass GraphSetup:\n    \"\"\"Handles the setup and configuration of the agent graph.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        quick_thinking_llm: Any,\n        deep_thinking_llm: Any,\n        conditional_logic: ConditionalLogic,\n        max_tool_rounds: int,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Initialize with required components.\"\"\"\n        self.quick_thinking_llm = quick_thinking_llm\n        self.deep_thinking_llm = deep_thinking_llm\n        self.conditional_logic = conditional_logic\n        self.max_tool_rounds = max_tool_rounds\n\n    def setup_graph(\n        self,\n        selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\", \"options\"),\n        memory_node=None,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Set up and compile the agent workflow graph.\n\n        Args:\n            selected_analysts (list): List of analyst types to include. Options are:\n                - \"market\": Market analyst\n                - \"social\": Sentiment analyst\n                - \"news\": News analyst\n                - \"fundamentals\": Fundamentals analyst\n                - \"options\": Options analyst\n            memory_node: Node that settles past decisions and returns the run's\n                ``past_context``. It runs alongside the analysts.\n        \"\"\"\n        plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analysts)\n\n        analyst_factories = {\n            \"market\": lambda: create_market_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"social\": lambda: create_sentiment_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"news\": lambda: create_news_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"fundamentals\": lambda: create_fundamentals_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"options\": lambda: create_options_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n        }\n\n        bull_researcher_node = create_bull_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        bear_researcher_node = create_bear_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        research_manager_node = create_research_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n        trader_node = create_trader(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n\n        aggressive_analyst = create_aggressive_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        neutral_analyst = create_neutral_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        conservative_analyst = create_conservative_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        portfolio_manager_node = create_portfolio_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n\n        workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)\n\n        for spec in plan.specs:\n            workflow.add_node(spec.agent_node,\n                              _analyst_graph(spec, analyst_factories[spec.key](), self.max_tool_rounds))\n\n        workflow.add_node(\"Bull Researcher\", bull_researcher_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Bear Researcher\", bear_researcher_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Research Manager\", research_manager_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Trader\", trader_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Aggressive Analyst\", aggressive_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Neutral Analyst\", neutral_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Conservative Analyst\", conservative_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Portfolio Manager\", portfolio_manager_node)\n\n        # The analysts work at the same time; the research debate starts once\n        # every one of them has filed its report. The memory log settles past\n        # decisions alongside them: only the Portfolio Manager reads its lessons.\n        first_steps = [spec.agent_node for spec in plan.specs]\n        if memory_node is not None:\n            workflow.add_node(\"Memory Log\", memory_node)\n            first_steps.append(\"Memory Log\")\n        for node in first_steps:\n            workflow.add_edge(START, node)\n        workflow.add_edge(first_steps, \"Bull Researcher\")\n\n        # Both research-debate edges share the complete DEBATE_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n        for debate_node in (\"Bull Researcher\", \"Bear Researcher\"):\n            workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n                debate_node,\n                self.conditional_logic.should_continue_debate,\n                DEBATE_PATH_MAP,\n            )\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Research Manager\", \"Trader\")\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Trader\", \"Aggressive Analyst\")\n        # All three risk edges share the complete RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n        for risk_node in (\"Aggressive Analyst\", \"Conservative Analyst\", \"Neutral Analyst\"):\n            workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n                risk_node,\n                self.conditional_logic.should_continue_risk_analysis,\n                RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP,\n            )\n\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Portfolio Manager\", END)\n\n        return workflow",

        "output": "<path>E:\\CityU课程材料\\CS5351软工\\CS5351-Project\\TradingAgents\\src\\tradingagents\\agents\\structured.py</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: \"\"\"Shared helpers for invoking an agent with structured output and a graceful fallback.\n2: \n3: The Portfolio Manager, Trader, and Research Manager all follow the same\n4: canonical pattern:\n5: \n6: 1. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``\n7:    so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the provider does\n8:    not support structured output (rare; mostly older Ollama models), the\n9:    wrap is skipped and the agent uses free-text generation instead.\n10: 2. At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to\n11:    markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason\n12:    (malformed JSON from a weak model, transient provider issue), fall\n13:    back to a plain ``llm.invoke`` so the pipeline never blocks.\n14: \n15: Centralising the pattern here keeps the agent factories small and ensures\n16: all three agents log the same warnings when fallback fires.\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: import logging\n22: from collections.abc import Callable\n23: from typing import Any, TypeVar\n24: \n25: from pydantic import BaseModel\n26: \n27: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n28: \n29: T = TypeVar(\"T\", bound=BaseModel)\n30: \n31: # Schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool (the schema itself), so a\n32: # model that reaches for a search tool emits an unknown tool call and the whole\n33: # structured attempt is discarded for a free-text retry. Agents on this path\n34: # state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone\n35: # (#1130).\n36: NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (\n37:     \"Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools \"\n38:     \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n39: )\n40: \n41: \n42: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n43:     \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n44: \n45:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n46:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n47:     \"\"\"\n48:     try:\n49:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n50:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n51:         logger.warning(\n52:             \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n53:             \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n54:             agent_name, exc,\n55:         )\n56:         return None\n57: \n58: \n59: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n60:     \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n61: \n62:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n63:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n64:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n65:     \"\"\"\n66:     if structured_llm is None:\n67:         return None\n68:     try:\n69:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n70:         if result is None:\n71:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n72:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n73:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n74:             raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n75:         return result\n76:     except Exception as exc:\n77:         logger.warning(\n78:             \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n79:             agent_name, exc,\n80:         )\n81:         return None\n82: \n83: \n84: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n85:     structured_llm: Any | None,\n86:     plain_llm: Any,\n87:     prompt: Any,\n88:     render: Callable[[T], str],\n89:     agent_name: str,\n90: ) -> str:\n91:     \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n92:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n93:     if result is not None:\n94:         return render(result)\n95:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content\n\n(End of file - total 95 lines)\n</content>",
        "title": "src\\tradingagents\\agents\\structured.py",
        "metadata": {
          "preview": "\"\"\"Shared helpers for invoking an agent with structured output and a graceful fallback.\n\nThe Portfolio Manager, Trader, and Research Manager all follow the same\ncanonical pattern:\n\n1. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``\n   so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the opposing argument exists in history but has no prior reply and the current turn both references it and adds a substantive clause (not a bare restatement), count = progress.\n\nProgress = (signal 1 OR signal 2). Rephrasing = same evidence units reused **and** no new answer → no progress. Opening round: detector is **never consulted** (guaranteed \"both speak once\").\n\n**Where the reason is set:** the router returns `\"Research Manager\"` and the researcher/manager path records `termination_reason = \"No new evidence or first response in this round\"`. To keep the router pure, the reason is a module constant in `conditional_logic.py` and written into `investment_debate_state` by the **research-manager node** (it already rewrites that dict) when the stop was an early stop — distinguish early stop (count < 2*cap, even, no progress) from cap stop (count ≥ 2*cap). Cap stop records no early reason (it's the normal limit). This keeps all writes deterministic and testable.\n\n**Determinism & testability:** pure function of state strings → no model cost, fully offline; DEB-T1–T5 can script turns and assert route + reason.\n\n### Limitations & uncertainty / failure handling\n- **Semantic paraphrase escapes token heuristics.** \"Margins are thin\" vs \"profitability is weak\" share no unit → could be mis-scored. Mitigation: reply-marker signal + risk-list note; treat as **fail-open (continue)** when uncertain, never fail-closed.\n- **Numeric coincidence** (same number reused for a different fact) could falsely read as \"not new\". Acceptable: errs toward continuing (safe, cap still bounds).\n- **Fragile phrase matching** for \"reply\" detection. Keep the marker set small and documented; unknown phrasings simply yield \"no detected reply\" → continue, not stop.\n- **Failure handling:** any exception, missing keys, empty/odd state, non-string content → **continue the debate** (degrade to baseline cap-only behavior), log a warning. Never crash the router, never stop early on detector error. Cap always wins.\n- **Coupling to FEAT-05:** detector must not require paragraph IDs. The only nodes writing `investment_debate_state` are the two researchers and the Research Manager. So the \"decision\" must be computed where state can be persisted, and the router must consume that persisted result — not recompute independently.\n\nUnchanged items kept brief: FR-DEB-01 and DEB-T1–T5 verbatim; cap = `2 * max_debate_rounds` turns, cap wins; opening round never stops; judge only after a complete bull+bear pair; risk debate and FEAT-01 untouched; full history preserved.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Revised progress detector\n\n### Why the deterministic-only detector is rejected\nThe token/unit detector fails the cases you named, and FR-DEB-01 requires semantic judgement (\"evidence new to this debate\", \"first substantive reply\"), which lexical proxies cannot represent:\n\n| Case | Deterministic units/reply-markers | Verdict |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Revenue +10% earlier; **gross margin 10%** later | number \"10\" reused → looks NOT new | wrong: fact is new |\n| **New qualitative fact**, no number/entity/ID | no unit → looks NOT new | wrong: it is new |\n| Repeated fact **with new numbering/citation labels** | new label → looks new | wrong: it is repetition |\n| First substantive reply, **no reply marker** | no marker → looks NOT replied | wrong: it is a first reply |\n| Marker present but **repeats an earlier rebuttal** | marker → looks like reply | wrong: no progress |\n| **Same reply text** first-time in history A, already answered in history B | identical text, different truth | detector must be history-relative |\n\nI will **not** weaken the requirement to fit a heuristic. Recommendation: a **hybrid whose judgement step is semantic (model-based), with deterministic guards**.\n\n### Recommended approach: structured semantic judgement, hybrid-guarded\n\n**Judgement unit.** A single structured semantic evaluation over the **newest complete pair** vs. the **prior debate history for this run** (not a global rule): the model is asked, per side, two binary questions anchored to that history:\n- `new_evidence`: does this turn introduce a fact/observation **not already present in the prior history** (evaluated by meaning, not surface form)? Label each introduced fact with a short tag so repetition-vs-new is justified.\n- `first_reply`: does this turn give a **first substantive response** to a specific opposing argument that, in this history, had **no prior substantive response**? Must name the opposing argument it answers.\n\nBoth are **history-relative**, which is what makes the \"same reply text, different history\" case correct: the same text is `first_reply=true` in history A (argument unanswered there) and `first_reply=false` in history B (already answered).\n\n**Deterministic guards around the model:**\n- **G1 Opening round skipped** — detector never invoked for round one (both always speak).\n- **G2 Pair gate** — only after an even `count ≥ 2` (both spoke); odd counts never judged.\n- **G3 Cap precedence** — checked before any judgement; at `2*cap` the run stops as a cap stop regardless of judgement.\n- **G4 Label-strip normalisation** before sending to the judge: strip FEAT-05-style `[FUN-01]`/`OPT-02` labels and pure renumbering from the comparison view, so labels alone cannot fabricate \"new\" (repeated-fact-with-new-labels case).\n- **G5 Structured schema + validation** — the judgement returns a typed object; malformed/absent output becomes `UNKNOWN`, never a silent \"no progress\".\n- **G6 Fail-open to continue** — `UNKNOWN` or judge error → continue (see §2), the same way the baseline cap-only routing behaves. This is safe: the requirement is about ending stalls, and we only end on a **confirmed** `NO_PROGRESS`.\n\n### How the six named cases resolve\n- **Reused number, new fact** (10% revenue vs 10% margin): model judges `new_evidence=true` from meaning; the guard's number-stripping means the guard cannot veto; **progress**.\n- **New qualitative fact, no unit**: `new_evidence=true`; **progress**.\n- **Repeated facts, only new labels**: guard G4 removes labels; model sees identical facts → `new_evidence=false`; if also no first reply → `NO_PROGRESS` → stop (DEB-T2).\n- **First substantive reply without marker**: model asked about meaning, not markers → `first_reply=true`; **progress**.\n- **Marker but repeats earlier rebuttal**: model checks against history → `first_reply=false`, `new_evidence=false` → `NO_PROGRESS`.\n- **Same reply text, different history**: answered/related to that run's history only → correctly true then false.\n\n### Limitations, failure handling, costs\n- **Limitations:** semantic judgement is **probabilistic/nondeterministic**; can disagree with a human on borderline replies; adds latency. It is the only method faithful to the requirement's meaning; I am not substituting it away.\n- **Failure handling:** `UNKNOWN` on missing/invalid judgement, provider error, timeout, or empty history → **continue**; cap and speaker order preserved; a warning is logged. Deterministic guards G1–G4 still bound behaviour. No early stop on uncertainty.\n- **Extra model calls / tokens:** **one extra structured model call per judged complete pair** (round ≥ 2), using the **quick** tier. Input ≈ the pair text + prior debate history (bounded by run length); output is a small typed judgement. DEB acceptance runs use scripted/mocked judgement so offline tests carry **zero** live cost; real-run cost = `(rounds−1)` calls per run (e.g. cap 3 → ≤ 2 extra calls) plus history tokens. This must be approved as a deliberate, bounded cost.\n\n### Measured-quality requirement\nBecause a model is involved, correctness is validated on a **fixed labelled evaluation set** (not mocks), separate from offline plumbing tests — see §4.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Resolving the uncertainty contradiction\n\nThree explicit outcomes, produced by the judgement and consumed identically by routing and handoff:\n\n| Outcome | When | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `PROGRESS` | New evidence **or** first substantive reply detected | Continue (next speaker in order) |\n| `NO_PROGRESS` | Neither detected, judgement confident | Stop early: record reason, hand full history to manager |\n| `UNKNOWN` | Missing/invalid judgement, provider error, empty/odd history | Continue (fail-open); record `UNKNOWN` reason for observability, not as early stop |\n\n**Why confirmed repetition still stops (DEB-T2):** in DEB-T2 the judge returns a confident `NO_PROGRESS` (both sides repeat round-one facts/rebuttals) → stop after the complete round two, no round three. `UNKNOWN` does **not** stop.\n\n**Cap and speaker order under unavailable judgement:** cap is checked first (G3) and always wins; odd counts always route to the next speaker (G2, unaffected by judgement); `UNKNOWN` continues, so a broken judge degrades to **baseline cap-only behaviour**, never a premature stop and never an out-of-order speaker.\n\n---\n\n## 3. State flow (one decision result, persisted before the manager)\n\n**Single decision result** (a small immutable value, e.g. a `DebateProgress` with `outcome: PROGRESS|NO_PROGRESS|UNKNOWN` and `reason: str`). It is computed **once** and stored on state; routing reads the stored result; the manager preserves it. No independent recomputation.\n\nBecause routers cannot write state, the result is produced and persisted by a **node update**, in this precise sequence:\n\n1. **Bear researcher node** (the turn that completes a pair, `count` becomes even ≥ 2 and below cap): before returning its normal `investment_debate_state` update, it computes the judgement for the just-completed pair and stores the decision. It returns the usual debate-state fields **plus** `progress_outcome` and `progress_reason` (new optional `InvestDebateState` fields), leaving `history`/`bull_history`/`bear_history`/`current_response`/`count` exactly as today.\n2. **Router `should_continue_debate`** reads the **persisted** `count`, `current_response`, and `progress_outcome` from state — not a fresh judgement. Order: cap (count ≥ 2·cap → Research Manager) → odd/`current_response` starts with Bull → Bear; then if `progress_outcome == NO_PROGRESS` at a pair boundary → Research Manager; else obvious continuation. It never re-judges.\n3. **Research manager node** starts **after** the bear node's update has been applied (LangGraph applies a node's returned state before routing to the next node), so `progress_outcome`/`progress_reason` are **already on state before the manager executes**. The manager **reads and preserves** them in its rebuilt `investment_debate_state` rather than recomputing, and writes the early-stop reason into the debate state it returns. On early stop it copies the full `history` unchanged into the manager prompt (already the case at `research_manager.py:19`).\n4. **Final state / saved run log:** the manager's preserved fields flow into the returned state; `_log_state` (`trading_graph.py:448`) adds `progress_outcome` and `progress_reason` under `investment_debate_state`. `run_rating`, export and FEAT-01 all read existing keys only — additive.\n\n**Source of the round cap:** the **current run's config** via `get_config()[\"max_debate_rounds\"]` (process-wide `run_config` set at `TradingAgentsGraph.__init__`; same value the router's `self.max_debate_rounds` comes from, `conditional_logic.py:9`). ```text
I approve the revised high-level approach for the environment-preparation and tests-only stage, subject to the corrections below. This is not approval to implement production changes or approval of tests that have not yet been reviewed.

Continue directly on CS5351. Preserve FEAT-01 and the separate risk debate. Do not create a branch, worktree or PR, and do not commit or push.


Incorporate these corrections into the test specification:


1. Correct the judgement boundary and call count.


Invoke the judge only after a complete round satisfying 2 <= round < cap, equivalently an even count with 4 <= count < 2 * cap. Caps 1 and 2 require zero judge calls; cap 3 permits at most one. In general, at most max(0, cap - 2) judgement evaluations are scheduled.


Router and manager must not re-judge. A failed structured judgement should become UNKNOWN without an additional free-text judgement attempt. Distinguish logical judgement calls from any existing provider-level retries.


2. Preserve evidence and chronological meaning.


Never remove factual numbers, signs, percentages, currencies, units or dates. Preserve the original history exactly. Any comparison-view normalization must affect only explicitly recognized presentation/citation labels.


Evaluate the bull turn against earlier history, then the bear turn against that history plus the current bull turn. Cover a first substantive reply to the current opposing turn, as well as repetition within the same pair.


3. Define a precise structured contract.


Show the proposed fields, valid values, explicit uncertainty representation, and deterministic mapping to PROGRESS, NO_PROGRESS or UNKNOWN. Cover malformed, inconsistent, missing and uncertain results. A valid JSON response alone does not establish semantic correctness.


4. Keep state and configuration consistent.


Reuse the bear's existing quick LLM and its callbacks; do not construct a separate model client.


Correct the description of get_config(): it prefers run-scoped configuration and otherwise uses a process-wide fallback. Prefer passing the same cap used by ConditionalLogic through the permitted setup wiring, or demonstrate equivalent run-scoped isolation.


Tie each judgement to the round it evaluated, or use an equally explicit reset mechanism. Old NO_PROGRESS results must not stop a new round, the opening round, or a run whose current judgement failed.


The bear's returned state update must already contain the exact early-stop reason:
No new evidence or first response in this round


The manager preserves it without regenerating it. A normal cap stop must not be mislabeled as a no-progress stop.


5. Test the integration and actual judgement separately.


Retain DEB-T1–T5, full-history handoff, reason-before-manager, reason-after-manager, saved-JSON persistence, old-state compatibility and FEAT-01 regression coverage.


Add focused checks for call counts, stale decisions and isolation between runs with different caps. Check the reason in the published state before manager execution, not only after the manager finishes.


Prepare fixed semantic evaluation examples with proposed expected labels and brief rationales for my review. Do not describe them as human-approved before I review them. Include the six semantic counterexamples from the previous review.


A real-judge evaluation may be excluded from default offline tests, but it is still needed before claiming semantic acceptance. Propose its entry point and pass criteria. Do not run live TradingAgents model calls during this stage.


Proceed as follows:


A. Create or reuse a project-local .venv and install the project's development dependencies. Use the virtual environment's Python executable directly so PowerShell activation is unnecessary.


B. Before adding tests, run the existing offline suite and record the exact command and actual result. If the pre-change baseline fails, report the failures and stop before adding feature tests.


C. Add only the feature tests, evaluation fixtures/runner and factual evidence records. Do not change production source or existing test expectations, and do not add implementation stubs to make the new tests pass.


D. Run the new tests and report their expected failures against the unimplemented feature. Run the prior offline tests separately so intended new failures do not obscure regressions.


Show the test diff, structured contract, requirement-to-test mapping, proposed evaluation labels, exact commands and actual results. Stop for my explicit test approval before implementing anything in src/.
```

The router and manager never re-judge.\"\n+  },\n+  \"schema\": {\n+    \"type\": \"object\",\n+    \"additionalProperties\": false,\n+    \"required\": [\"bull\", \"bear\", \"outcome\"],\n+    \"properties\": {\n+      \"bull\": {\n+        \"type\": \"object\",\n+        \"additionalProperties\": false,\n+        \"required\": [\"new_evidence\", \"first_reply\", \"confidence\"],\n+        \"properties\": {\n+          \"new_evidence\": {\n+            \"type\": \"boolean\",\n+            \"description\": \"The bull turn introduces a fact/observation not already present in the prior debate history, judged by meaning (numbers, qualitative claims, or held/refuted points alike).\"\n+          },\n+          \"first_reply\": {\n+            \"type\": \"boolean\",\n+            \"description\": \"The bull turn gives a first substantive response to a specific opposing argument that had no prior substantive response in this history.\"\n+          },\n+          \"confidence\": {\n+            \"type\": \"string\",\n+            \"enum\": [\"low\", \"medium\", \"high\"],\n+            \"description\": \"The judge's confidence in the two booleans for this side.\"\n+          }\n+        }\n+      },\n+      \"bear\": {\n+        \"type\": \"object\",\n+        \"additionalProperties\": false,\n+        \"required\": [\"new_evidence\", \"first_reply\", \"confidence\"],\n+        \"properties\": {\n+          \"new_evidence\": {\n+            \"type\": \"boolean\",\n+            \"description\": \"The bear turn introduces a fact/observation not already present in the prior history plus the current bull turn.\"\n+          },\n+          \"first_reply\": {\n+            \"type\": \"boolean\",\n+            \"description\": \"The bear turn gives a first substantive response to a bull point that had no prior substantive response, including a first reply within the same pair.\"\n+          },\n+          \"confidence\": {\n+            \"type\": \"string\",\n+            \"enum\": [\"low\", \"medium\", \"high\"]\n+          }\n+        }\n+      },\n+      \"outcome\": {\n+        \"type\": \"string\",\n+        \"enum\": [\"PROGRESS\", \"NO_PROGRESS\", \"UNKNOWN\"],\n+        \"description\": \"The judge may also return UNKNOWN directly when it cannot decide.\"\n+      }\n+    }\n+  },\n+  \"deterministic_mapping\": {\n+    \"rule\": \"outcome_of(judgement) is computed by the node, not taken on trust if inconsistent.\",\n+    \"steps\": [\n+      \"If the structured call fails, returns None, or the payload is not an object with the required keys -> UNKNOWN.\",\n+      \"If any confidence is 'low' for a side whose flags are all false (i.e. we would otherwise stop on that side's weakness) -> UNKNOWN (do not stop on a weak negative).\",\n+      \"If the payload's own outcome field contradicts the booleans (PROGRESS with all flags false, or NO_PROGRESS with any flag true) -> UNKNOWN (inconsistent).\",\n+      \"PROGRESS if any of bull.new_evidence, bull.first_reply, bear.new_evidence, bear.first_reply is true.\",\n+      \"NO_PROGRESS only if all four flags are false AND both sides' confidence is at least 'medium' AND the outcome field agrees.\",\n+      \"Anything else -> UNKNOWN.\"\n+    ]\n+  },\n+  \"failure_handling\": {\n+    \"unknown\": \"Continue the debate (fail open). The round cap and speaker order are unchanged; the persisted outcome is UNKNOWN with an empty early-stop reason.\",\n+    \"no_freetext_retry\": \"A failed structured judgement becomes UNKNOWN once. The judge is never retried as free text. Provider/SDK-level transport retries (existing client behaviour) are not judgement attempts and are not counted as such.\"\n+  }\n+}\n",

\"risk_debate_state\": _risk_state(),\n         **extra,\n         \"investment_debate_state\": debate,\n     }\n \n \n def _risk_state():\n     \"\"\"A minimal risk-debate state so _log_state can \"latest_speaker\": \"\",\n         \"current_aggressive_response\": \"\",\n         \"current_conservative_response\": \"\",\n         \"current_neutral_response\": \"\",\n         \"count\": 0,\n fixed turn (the judge is separate).\"\"\"\n     llm = MagicMock()\n     llm.invoke.side_effect = lambda prompt: (\n         captured.__setitem__(\"prompt\", prompt) or MagicMock(content=content)\n     )\n     return llm\n \n \n def _router(max_rounds):\n     return ConditionalLogic(max_debate_rounds=max_rounds)\n \n \n # --- routing is determined by the persisted result, never recomputed --------\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_router_returns_only_known_debate_targets():\n     \"\"\"FR-DEB-01: the router's return set stays inside DEBATE_PATH_MAP.\"\"\"\n     logic = _router(max_rounds=3)\n y\", \"\", \"drift\")\n         for count in (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)\n     }\n     assert returns <= set(DEBATE_PATH_MAP)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_debate_path_map_is_unchanged():\n     \"\"\"FR-DEB-01/FEAT-02: no new edge targets are introduced.\"\"\"\n     assert set(DEBATE_PATH_MAP) == {\n         \"Bull Researcher\",\n         \"Bear Researcher\",\n         \"Research Bull then bear speak once and\n     round two begins (no early stop on the opening round).\"\"\"\n     logic = _router(max_rounds=3)\n \n     after_bull = logic.should_continue_debate(\n         _state(_debate_state(current_response=\"Bull Analyst: opening\", count=1))\n     )\n     assert after_bull == \"Bear Researcher\"\n \n     after_bear = logic.should_continue_debate(\n         _state(_debate_state(current_response=\"Bear Analyst: opening\", count=2))\n     )\n     assert after_bear == \"Bull Researcher\"\n \n \n # --- DEB-T2: confirmed repetition in round two stops -----------------------\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n+def test_after_bull_speaks_in_round_two_the_bear_still_gets_a_turn():\n+    \"\"\"FR-DEB-01: one round is one bull turn and one bear turn. The bear\n     still speaks; then, with a persisted NO_PROGRESS for this round, the router\n     hands off instead of starting round three.\"\"\"\n     logic = _router(max_rounds=3)\n \n     after_bull = logic.should_continue_debate(\n         _state(_debate_state(\n             current_response=\"Bull Analyst: repeats\",\n             count=3,\n             progress_outcome=OUTCOME_NO_PROGRESS,\n             progress_round=2,\n         ))\n     )\n     assert after_bull == \"Bear Researcher\"\n \n     after_bear = logic.should_continue_debate(\n         _state(_debate_state(\n             current_response=\"Bear Analyst: repeats\",\n             count=4,\n             progress_outcome=OUTCOME_NO_PROGRESS,\n             progress_round=2,\n         ))\n     )\n     assert after_bear == \"Research Manager\"\n \n \n # --- DEB-T3 / DEB-T4: progress in round two continues ----------------------\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"outcome\", [OUTCOME_PROGRESS])\n def test_deb_t3_new_report_fact_continues_to_round_three(outcome):\n     \"\"\"DEB-T3: limit 3; round two adds a report fact. A persisted PROGRESS keeps\n     the debate going into round three.\"\"\"\n     logic = _router(max_rounds=3)\n     target = logic.should_continue_debate(\n         _state(_debate_state(\n             current_response=\"Bear Analyst: new fact\",\n             count=4,\n             progress_outcome=outcome,\n             progress_round=2,\n         ))\n     )\n     assert target == \"Bull Researcher\"\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_deb_t4_first_reply_continues_to_round_three():\n     \"\"\"DEB-T4: limit 3; round two answers an unanswered opposing point. It never imports ``tradingagents.graph``.\n+\n+FR-DEB-01 says the debate ends early when neither side introduces evidence new\n+to this debate nor gives a first substantive reply to a previously unanswered\n+opposing argument. pair, in the bear node.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import logging\n+from dataclasses import dataclass\n+from typing import Literal\n+\n+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field\n+\n+from tradingagents.agents.structured import NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS\n+\n+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n+\n+PROGRESS = \"PROGRESS\"\n+NO_PROGRESS = \"NO_PROGRESS\"\n+UNKNOWN = \"UNKNOWN\"\n+\n+# The exact approved early-stop reason (FR-DEB-01 / FEAT-02 blueprint).\n+EARLY_STOP_REASON = \"No new evidence or first response in this round\"\n+\n+_CONFIDENCE_RANK = {\"low\": 0, \"medium\": 1, \"high\": 2}\n+\n+\n+class _SideJudgement(BaseModel):\n+    new_evidence: bool = Field(\n+        description=\"True if this turn introduces a fact/observation not already \"\n+        \"present in the prior debate history, judged by meaning, whether numeric \"\n+        \"or qualitative.\"\n+    )\n+    first_reply: bool = Field(\n+        description=\"True if this turn gives a \"medium\", \"high\"] = Field(\n+        description=\"Confidence in the two booleans for this side.\"\n+    )\n+\n+\n+class DebateJudgement(BaseModel):\n+    \"\"\"Structured judgement for one completed bull/bear pair.\"\"\"\n+\n+    bull: _SideJudgement\n+    bear: _SideJudgement\n+    outcome: Literal[\"PROGRESS\", \"NO_PROGRESS\", \"UNKNOWN\"]\n+\n+\n+@dataclass(frozen=True)\n+class ProgressResult:\n+    outcome: str\n+    evaluated_round: int\n+\n+\n+def _flags_any_true(side) -> bool:\n+    return bool(side[\"new_evidence\"] or side[\"first_reply\"])\n+\n+\n+def
